newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France group plans new express unit.
newsitem.headline: Air France group plans new express unit.

text.p: The Air France group plans to create a new parcel express division when Air France and the former Air Inter (now Air France Europe) merge next April 1, the carrier's director general Sten Grotenfelt said.
He told Reuters in an interview that it was his intention to fold their respective express delivery activities along with their sizeable postal delivery interests into an integrated operation.
"We want to take part of this market," he said.

"With our present network we can compete with people like Federal Express and DHL to some extent... We can also compete positively to certain destinations. We already do some of their business," he added.
He said that Air France intended to expand its sales and marketing activities in the express field but would not create any new corporate structures.

This would bring the new cargo group's employee head count to around 3,000, which he expected to stay unchanged. Initially about 2,750 staff will be from the old Air Inter and 250 from Air France Cargo, he said.

"What we're trying to do is expand our activities without increasing the number of employees. The only job losses will be under the company's voluntary retirement programme which will entail some rotation of people but no change in numbers," he added.

Air France is also working on bar-coding of cargo and airway bills under the umbrella of an IATA worling group. Bar coding was so far only used on express deliveries, "but not on general cargo," Grotenfelt said.

"It will play an important part in our new Charles de Gaulle (CDG) cargo complex in helping to improve our quality. We are, however, putting coding on pallets which will help. But on cargo and airway bills we should be testing bar-coding on cargo in about two years," he added.
Grotenfelt said Air France did not favour the creation of the dedicated Paris cargo airport being mooted for either Vatry or Chateauroux.
"Having directed Fedex to CDG, it would be a bit strange for the government to tell Air France to go somewhere else," he noted.
With so much capacity in passenger aircraft tied to CDG, such a facility would deny Air France the flexibility needed to stay competitive, he said.
